metadata.case_name: HONG KONG RED CROSS v. THE HONG KONG FEDERATION OF YOUTH GROUPS

plaintiff.occupation_before: teacher at the Plaintiff’s North District Hospital Red Cross School (Hong Kong Red Cross Hospital School)

source: These findings were consistent with back sprain.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: maximum duration for her to either sit, stand or walk was 10 – 15 minutes
recurrent exacerbations of back pain requiring wheelchair for outdoor activities during those periods
local tenderness over 4th and 5th lumbar regions; diminished spinal movements; only mildly positive straight leg raising tests; no motor-sensory deficits
muscle guarding and mild spasm over the lumbar region and tenderness over both iliac crests and midline of the lumbar spine particularly over the lumbosacral junction

treatments_received.treatment: Accident and Emergency assessment and analgesic
source: he was taken to the Accident and Emergency Department of Tseung Kwan O Hospital where Dr. Kung Shu Wing found positive sign of tenderness on her lower back region. X-ray of the lumbascaral region did not show any fractures, his diagnosis was ‘back contussion’ and Miss Chan was given analgesic and sent home.

treatments_received.treatment: Admission to orthopaedic ward and physiotherapy
source: On 5 June 2002, Miss Chan suffered great pain and attended the Queen Elizabeth Hospital and was admitted into the orthopaedic ward.
Her physiotherapy treatments included manual therapy and ultrasonic treatments.
MRI was taken and the doctors found only multiple sacral meningeal cysts which, according to the doctors, were usually harmless and asymptomatic.

treatments_received.treatment: Orthopaedic specialist consultations (Professor Leung, Dr. Johnson C.K. Lam and others)
source: Miss Chan was examined by Professor Leung Ping Chung of the Chinese University Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department appointed by the Federation and Dr. Johnson C.K. Lam, specialist in Orthopaedics & Traumatology.

Dr. Johnson Lam’s medical report of 13 January 2005 revealed Miss Chan had consulted a private Orthopaedic specialist at the Baptist Hospital and later Dr. Chau Yat Sang on 1 August 2003 for back pain and knee pain after exercise.

treatments_future.treatment: ongoing physiotherapy 2 to 3 times a week
source: At the time of the trial, 7½ years after the accident, she was still attending regular physiotherapy treatments 2 to 3 times a week and she would experience acute inflammation causing constant pain on her low back every now and then.

losses.description: Persistent low back pain and reduced spinal function with tenderness, diminished spinal movements and intermittent exacerbations limiting ability to sit, stand or walk for more than short periods.
Unable to return to pre-accident occupation as a teacher of sick children at the hospital and assessed loss of earning capacity (6%).
